source_text:
Τοῦ δὲ κατὰ Λουκᾶν
ὑπὸ Λουκᾶ μαθητοῦ ὑπάρχοντος τοῦ ἀποστόλου Παύλου, οὗ μνημονεύων ὁ αὐτὸς
ἀπόστολος ἔν τινι ἐπιστολῇ γράφει· ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Λουκᾶς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἰατρός, καὶ
τὰς πράξεις δὲ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων ὁ αὐτὸς εὐαγγελιστὴς συνεγράψατο. Οὔτε
πλείονα τῶν ἀριθμῶν, οὔτε ἐλάττονα ἐνδέχεται αὐτὰ γενέσθαι. Τὸ μὲν γὰρ κατὰ
Ἰωάννην εὐαγγέλιον τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡγεμωνικὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ πρακτικὴν καὶ
ἔνδοξον γενεὰν 130 διηγεῖται· ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ
θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος, πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο· διὰ τοῦτο εἰς ὁμοίωμα ἀετοῦ. Τὸ δὲ κατὰ
Λουκᾶν ἅτε ἀπὸ ἱερατικοῦ χαρακτῆρος ὑπάρχων ἀπὸ Ζαχαρίου ἤρξατο τοῦ ἱερέως
λέγων· ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρώδου, τοῦ βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἱερεύς τις
ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβία, ἐπειδὴ κατὰ τὴν παλαιὰν τοῦ νόμου
παράδοσιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ταύρους ἐκόμιζον· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ὡς μοσχόμορφον
ἀνιστορίζεται.
orientation: The author is explaining the symbolic character of each Gospel, and has just described John's Gospel as the eagle; now he turns to Luke's Gospel and its opening with the priest Zechariah.
pass_a_gloss: But the Gospel according to Luke, Luke being a disciple of the apostle Paul, whom the same apostle remembering writes in a certain letter: 'Luke the beloved physician greets you,' and the acts of the holy apostles the same evangelist composed. Neither more than the numbers, nor fewer, is it possible for them to be. For the Gospel according to John narrates his princely and active and glorious generation from the Father: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and God was the Word; all things came to be through him'; for this reason into the symbol of an eagle. But the Gospel according to Luke, since it is from a priestly character, began from Zechariah the priest, saying: 'There was in the days of Herod, king of Judea, a certain priest named Zechariah of the division of Abijah,' since according to the old tradition of the law the priests brought bulls; for this reason also its form is depicted as calf-shaped.

choices.why: Matches the fixed glossary sense for Luke as beloved physician and keeps the adjective-noun order of the source

choices.term: τὰς πράξεις δὲ τῶν ἁγίων ἀποστόλων
choices.english: the acts of the holy apostles
choices.why: Literal rendering of πράξεις as acts, preserving the source's term for the book of Acts
rejected: the deeds of the holy apostles
the Acts of the holy apostles

choices.why: Renders the adjective literally as princely, conveying ruling or sovereign character of the generation from the Father
Literal compound rendering of μοσχόμορφον, preserving the calf symbol from the glossary
rejected: in the form of a calf

choices.why: Renders the verb as depicted, conveying the visual representation of the Gospel's form

bible_refs.note: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Λουκᾶς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἰατρός
ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος, πάντα δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο
ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡρώδου, τοῦ βασιλέως τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ἱερεύς τις ὀνόματι Ζαχαρίας ἐξ ἐφημερίας Ἀβία

pass_b_english: The Gospel according to Luke, however, belongs to Luke, a disciple of the apostle Paul. The same apostle remembers him and writes in a certain letter, “Luke, the beloved physician, greets you” (Colossians 4:14). This same evangelist also composed the acts of the holy apostles. These gospels cannot be more or fewer than this number. For the Gospel according to John recounts his princely, active, and glorious generation from the Father: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God; all things came into being through him” (John 1:1, 3). For this reason it bears the symbol of the eagle. The Gospel according to Luke, since it has a priestly character, begins with Zechariah the priest, saying, “In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah” (Luke 1:5), because according to the old tradition of the law the priests brought bulls. For this reason its form is depicted as calf-shaped.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡγεμωνικὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ πρακτικὴν καὶ ἔνδοξον γενεὰν
last_rejected.why: ἡγεμωνικὴν means 'ruling/governing' not 'princely'; γενεὰν refers to 'origin/birth' not 'generation' in modern sense.
last_rejected.fix: his ruling, active, and glorious origin from the Father
last_rejected.ruling: ἡγεμωνικὴν 'princely' and γενεὰν 'generation' are within normal semantic range; no meaning lost or misled.

last_rejected.why: ταύρους means 'bulls/oxen' but context is sacrificial animals; however, the symbol is μόσχος (calf), and the point is priests brought calves/young cattle for sacrifice, not mature bulls.
last_rejected.ruling: ταύρους correctly means 'bulls'; source says bulls, not calves. Translation faithfully renders the Greek word used.
